I know for sure that we received information that none of the units had any HVO prisoners and that all the prisoners there were were accommodated in the prison in Zenica, in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "after the negotiations," I'm just interested in the time frame in which this query was sent out. Was a query sent out on one occasion following or during one set of negotiations, or was this a regular and ongoing process whereby you were constantly asking the brigades and battalions if they had prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Every time when the other side and, in this case, the HVO commission presented some information during the negotiations, we would endeavour to check that information on our part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on how many of those occasions were you able to determine that brigades or battalions of the 3rd Corps of the ABiH were keeping surrendered HVO soldiers in their custody?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said: "Every time when the HVO commission presented some information during negotiations, we would endeavour to check that information." Following these checks that you made, on how many occasions did you determine that brigades or battalions of the 3rd Corps of the ABiH were keeping surrendered HVO soldiers in custody?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe, sir, earlier this morning, you told us that you personally were never involved in the exchange of any foreigners.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document you have in front of you, P655, the bottom half of that document where it says, "we would get the following of our men in exchange." Do you see that portion?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I do indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read out what it says under number 6.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes. And I can also clarify, if I may.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: This is a list which was offered by the HVO commission during the exchange. And when I talked to my commander, I could tell him who were the prisoners kept by the HVO and offered by the HVO commission. As far as I can remember, when Mr. Alagic looked at this particular list, he said: "Who is this? Who is this Hasan Beganovic?" And I said: "This is a man from the 312th." And then he asked me who Kasim Arnautovic was. And then I explained because I knew which units these people belonged to. And when we arrived at Mustafa Kohal, I told him I didn't have a clue who it was; it was them who offered him in exchange. His reply was "I'm not interested in foreigners." Once the exchange was implemented according to this principle - I don't know whether you have this document or not - but I know that there are always reports issued by the exchanges commission on every exchange. We gave up on this Syrian. We didn't want to have him exchanged, and I never know to this very day who this person was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, sir, from this answer that if the HVO proposed exchanging foreigners, Mr. Beba would not agree to that?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Again, I didn't understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, maybe my learned friend misspoke, because the witness has mentioned his conversation with Mr. Alagic rather than with Mr. Beba.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that is correct. Let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you spoke with Mr. Alagic, if you presented Mr. or General Alagic with a list that included foreigners, he would not agree to the exchange if the HVO was proposing to exchange foreigners?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this was the only time when a foreigner was offered for exchange. In this particular case, Alagic was categorical when he said no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the bottom left-hand part of this page. There is some -- there's a handwritten word and a signature. Can you tell us what that says and tell us if you recognise that handwriting.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: At the bottom, it says "in agreement, Beba Salko." And in the right top corner, it says "I approve, Commander Alagic."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused, then, sir, because you've told us that Mr. Alagic was categorical when he said no to this exchange, but now you're telling us that at the top right-hand portion of this page, it says "I approve, Commander Alagic"?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Let me explain. I took this report personally to Mr. Alagic. My office was very close to the command of the operations group. I spoke to him, and he asked for some clarifications. You may have noticed here under 7, I explained to him which HVO prisoner is this relative to. I provided him with verbal explanations, and he verbally told me that he did not approve the exchange of this Syrian and he approved everything else. That is why I proceeded with the exchange very soon after the negotiations. I used this same list, but I omitted the Syrian. The Syrian was not part of the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would the document, to the best of your recollection, would you have taken this first to Commander Alagic or first to Mr. Beba?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I believe that I first went to Mr. Alagic. He then referred me to Mr. Beba. He was in the position to tell me if there was anything else, any other reason for which not all of the HVO prisoners could be exchanged. However, Mr. Beba was agreeable, and he confirmed his agreement by putting his signature on this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during the time period in 1993 when you were involved in general with prisoner exchanges, did you ever have any instance where you were involved with exchanging civilians?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: As I've already stated, I had a very close relationship with the civilian commission. That is, the state municipal commission in Travnik. We shared the office. And we acted together during the exchanges. I was the one in charge of the prisoners of war. However, sometimes the civilians would be exchanged in the same place as the prisoners of war, the military prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, let me move on to a different topic, but one which is slightly related. During the period in 1993 when you were involved in exchanging prisoners, that is, soldiers, not civilians but soldiers, did there ever come a time when any of the civilian authorities in the area that you were dealing with were at any point in time were civilian authorities holding prisons, HVO prisons, surrendered HVO prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to be clear then, at no point in time are you aware of the civilian authorities having any involvement in prisoner exchanges or having a veto over prisoner exchanges during 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. I know that some HVO prisoners were set free, that criminal charges were issued, and that they would be transferred to the authority of the municipal court. What happened to them after that, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you at any point in time in 1993, did your duties or responsibilities include any type of questioning or interrogation of captured HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher, I would ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P105. And again, Mr. President, we do have extra copies for everyone in and around the courtroom if that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you if you've ever seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me turn your attention, then, sir, to paragraph 5 of this document. According to paragraph 5 of this document, yourself along with Mr. Eminovic and Mr. Beba who you've previously told us were involved with the exchange commissions were responsible for checkpoints, control of checkpoints in the OG Bosanska Krajina zone of responsibility. Sir, was that, in fact, the case as of 28 June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: As I've already said, I've never seen this order before. I was never in charge of any checkpoints. Maybe Salko had the idea that I should help them or something. However, I never received this order. I never performed controls at any of the checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let me ask you this, then, sir: Were you ever verbally ordered to control checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take a look, please, at the signature on page 2 of this document, and I would ask you, sir, if you recognise that signature.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I think that this is Commander Alagic's signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, sir, turning to paragraph 5 of the document, we see your name, Samir Sefer, and it says "operations group security officer." And it's your testimony that in at no point in time in 1993, including 28 June 1993, at no point in time were you a security officer in operational group Bosanska Krajina. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes. And I adhere by that statement. I was never involved in the security of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question, sir, at any point in time in 1993 - and the documents can be returned to the Registrar - at any point in 1993 during the period of time that you were involved in exchange commissions, did you have any personal contact with any of the foreigners, such as the Mujahedin or what were often called the Arabs? Did you have any personal contact with those people in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I did not have any personal contacts with them. On a couple of occasions, I saw a foreigner come into the commission for exchanges. And this foreigner spoke to Mr. Beba.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at what point in time would that be, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact date. It could have been sometime in October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this foreigner who came into the commission for exchanges sometime in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I don't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no further questions for the witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few questions, Mr. President. Re-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll ask Mr. Sefer about his position when this foreigner came to the office of the commission for exchanges and spoke to Mr. Beba.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: This was in October. I was a member of the municipal commission for exchanges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. So it was not a mistake when you said that this was in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Document Number P655, the Prosecution Exhibit 655.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your capacity as the president of this commission, after the exchanges, were you duty-bound to draft a report and submit information on the persons who had been exchanged?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes. I was duty-bound to draft a report on the negotiations as well as on the exchanges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said to my learned friend that the person under item 6 called Mustafa Kohal, a Syrian, was not included into the exchange that was carried out after these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: That is correct. He was not included.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the others? Were they exchanged? Were they recorded in your report on the exchange?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes, and yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the usher please show the witness the following document. We have a sufficient number of copies for everybody. I apologise, Your Honours. We have not shown this document to the witness because it was not on our exhibit list. It is the document that we thought might be used during his examination. This document will appear on our supplemental list. However, since my learned friend showed this witness his Exhibit P655, I would kindly ask permission for this witness to be shown documents that arise from the exchange and a report on this particular exchange. May the witness please be shown these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just note at this point for the record that this obviously is the first time we've seen this document. We were, of course, given no advance notice of any documents to be shown to this witness. And I may feel it necessary, Mr. President, at some point in the near future to address the Chamber on this issue. But for the time being, I will simply note that this document has just been produced for the Prosecution, and I'll leave it at that for now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have not disclosed this document to the Prosecution? You've just done it this very moment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we did mention to the Prosecution that we might be in the position to use this document, and it was prepared. However, it was not on the list, and we didn't plan for this document to be used today. This document is part of those documents that we will submit to the Trial Chamber before the 3rd of December. However, on his cross-examination, the Prosecutor used a document which preceded these documents that I have here on me. I thought it would be appropriate at this point in time to show this document -- these documents. If the Trial Chamber believes it is not appropriate, I will leave these documents for some subsequent witnesses, but these are the documents drafted by this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're saying that you had this document, and you forgot to put it on your list or something to that effect. But you were going to do it at a later stage because the list is not going to be complete before the 3rd of December. And since the Prosecutor has put questions regarding these exchanges on his cross-examination, you want to show these documents to the witness because they were drafted by him. And he is aware of those documents, and that is why you want this witness to be shown these documents. Is that correct? Mr. Mundis, regarding the relevance, the Defence has explained how come the document was not on this particular list. They were going to put it on the list. They didn't. What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, as the Chamber is aware, yesterday we were told that if there were to be any documents to be shown to the witness, that that would be communicated to us by 5.00 p.m. I do note that this document was drafted by and has the signature of this witness on it. And he was involved in prisoner exchanges, and this document relates to prisoner exchanges. I'm not necessarily at this point, Mr. President, objecting to the document, but I am objecting to the way in which this document has now appeared before this witness following our cross-examination of the witness. Had we been aware or had they used this document in direct, we certainly wouldn't have had any problems whatsoever or had that been communicated by us by 5.00 p.m. yesterday afternoon. I'm simply informing the Chamber of this problem so that hopefully it won't recur in the future, but also to reserve our position in the event we do need to address the Trial Chamber later with respect to this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Defence counsel has taken note of what has been said. But please proceed and put your question to the witness on the basis of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sefer, please have a look at the document, the date of which is the 15th of August 1993. And then the document dated the 16th of August 1993. Are these documents that you yourself drafted?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these documents follow on the negotiations with the HVO representatives? They follow on the documents presented to you by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at the document dated the 16th of August 1993. The number of the document is 01-114/93. Could you tell me whether this is a report on an exchange that you carried out with HVO representatives?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes. This is my report on that exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this list, could we have the name of the individual whose name is Kohal Mustafa and who is a Syrian?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No, he's not included in this list.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other questions, Mr. President. And I would like to tender this document into evidence. We will give it the appropriate number, the next number on our list of exhibits if it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We only have a few questions for this witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Ibrisimovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When cross-examined by the Prosecution, you were asked whether you were involved in the exchange of one called Kadiric Ensud?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you knew this person and that you were involved in that exchange.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when this took place?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, as I said, it was perhaps at the beginning of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to show the witness a document we received from our colleagues from the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 68. It's a statement made by this person who was exchanged, a statement given at the police station of the military police in Vitez. Could the usher please show the witness this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could actually be either shown what this document is or perhaps given a little bit more information about what the document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only have one copy in English and one in B/C/S. We received this document from the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 68. It's a statement made by Mr. Kadiric, and I think his name was mentioned in the course of the examination of the witness. I assume that my colleagues have this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the person named Kadiric, Emsud, is that the person who gave the statement? Is that the person who was exchanged, and did you participate in that exchange?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this person was captured, which unit was he a member of? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, I found out that he had been captured at a very late date. I found out that he was in the hands of the HVO and that he was in the Kaonik prison. And this is information I obtained through the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have a look at the statement, he claims that he was a member of the El Mujahedin unit.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes. Later in the course of the exchange, he said that he was a member of the El Mujahid unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Could we see the English version of the document so we can follow it. We don't have that version. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since we received this document from the Prosecution, we would like to tender it into evidence. We received it pursuant to Rule 68, but we have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have some questions that relate to Document P655, and then questions relating the document shown by the Defence, the document dated the 15th of August. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, in the document dated the 13th of July 1993, the documents you have before you, this is a document that you yourself drafted. You say in this document that on the 12th of July, radio contact was established with HVO representatives. And furthermore, the HVO representatives requested that the POW exchange take place at 1700 hours on the 13th of July. Apparently, in Dolac. Is that, in fact, what it says in the document that you drafted?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently, radio contact was established. So were radiosets used or telephones? Was a radio frequency used or was it something like a Motorola device that was used for contact?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, it was a radioset. I already mentioned how I established contact with the HVO commission. And there was a radioset that ElektroTravnik company, and ElektroVitez company also had a similar device.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I have understood this correctly, the list of prisoners from 1 to 12, Filipovic -- from Filipovic to the person who was in Mehurici, if I understood you correctly, who listed the names? Did the HVO provide you with these names, or did you write down these names?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, all the names here were provided by the HVO. And it's the HVO that made this suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the HVO knew that there were seven individuals detained in Travnik. There were eight, in fact, who were in Travnik. There were three who were apparently in the Zenica hospital. And one was in Mehurici. Was the HVO very well informed about the situation within the ABiH? Did they have first-hand and reliable information?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: As far as the names mentioned here are concerned, and with regard to the HVO members who were detained by the ABiH, well, they had reliable information about these affairs. Because in our prisoners -- we allowed the International Red Cross to gain access to our prisons and to the hospital. The Red Cross could register the names of the HVO and the detainees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the names you were provided with, did these names mean anything to you? You mentioned Stipo Filipovic, or you referred to someone called Stipo Filipovic. Did you know this person or not?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So under number 7, Bonic, how is it that you mention when he was arrested he had an amputated ear with him? How were you aware of this fact.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, the entire town was familiar with this fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The entire town knew about it. As far as the other 12 names are concerned, the BHA soldiers, we have Hasan Beganovic, who is mentioned as the first one, and Fahrudin Hadzalic is the last one on that list, did they provide you with their names?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes, they provided the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Salko Beba and Alagic approved the document, did that entail an agreement for the exchange that was to take place at 1700 hours on the 13th of July? You've said naturally that Mustafa Kohal was excluded from this exchange.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that Mustafa Kohal shouldn't be included in the exchange. I was told that we weren't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 13th of July at 1700 hours, did this exchange actually take place?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I have to provide you with a somewhat lengthy explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I was involved in a large number of exchanges, especially a large number of exchanges with the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor. The exchanges that I was involved in with the HVO caused so many difficulties that once an agreement has been reached on an exchange, you can nevertheless not be sure that the exchange will actually take place. It happened very frequently. For example, Ivica Saric is mentioned here. Just after having reached an agreement with Ivica Saric about the exchange, information would arrive according to which it wasn't possible to carry out the exchange. They said, we've got a new man, we've replaced a man, and then you would have to negotiate with him. And then I would be told to negotiate with Mr. Nikica Petrovic. And after discussed the matter with him on numerous occasions, and after having reached another agreement, a third person would suddenly appear on the scene, and this is why this exchange took place at a later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. When did you realise you couldn't carry out the exchange at 1700 hours -- when you actually realised this couldn't be carried out, did you phone the HVO to agree on carrying out the exchange at a later date?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, after I had reached an agreement on this exchange, they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm referring to this specific case, to this particular exchange. When did you inform the HVO that it couldn't take place at 1700 hours on the 13th of July in Dolac?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, I didn't inform them. They informed me that this exchange could not be carried out in this way. They thought that everyone should be exchanged for everyone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they contacted you via radiolink. They said that when you carried out the exchange, 12 men should be exchanged on one side for 12 men on the other?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No. I'll correct this. They didn't contact me via radiolink to inform me that there would be no exchange on that occasion. But I was informed of this by the International Red Cross. They had probably been to see them, and we wouldn't have got involved in small-scale exchanges. We were told that they wanted to exchange all the men on one side for all the men on the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you said that this was information provided via the International Red Cross. Have a look at Document 655. There's no number on the document. The document dated the 15th of August has a number, but this document, Document 655, doesn't have a number under which it was registered. Do you have an explanation? I'm referring to the document that the Defence provided you with a minute ago. The number of this document is 01-112/93. And there is a date. So it's a military-style document. But the other document I'm referring to doesn't have a number under which it was registered. Why?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Because it's just information on the negotiations conducted. It's not an official report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Still referring to Document 655 now, it contains your name, and we can also see a sort of heart with the symbol of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there is a cross. Why is there a cross next to the coat of arms? Was this to give -- was this in order to recognise the fact that the Red Cross was involved in the exchange?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes. The red cross was the symbol used by the International Red Cross. It symbolises the humanitarian work that they were involved in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, how is it that we can't see this sign in the document dated the 15th of August? You see the stamp is different, and there's no red cross.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, let me explain this. When returning from the negotiations, I returned to my office and drafted a report on the negotiations conducted, and then I stamped the document with the stamp of the commission for exchanges. On the other document, the stamp is different because our imprisoned members were exchanged. I took them to the clinic in the barracks for an examination. And in the OG command, I drafted a report on the exchange of POWs. And I then stamped the document with the OG group's stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When comparing the two documents, the document dated the 15th of August makes reference to the International Red Cross and to UNPROFOR. It contains these references. However, on the document dated the 13th of July, no such references are contained. Weren't there any official exchanges with the International Red Cross and exchanges of a different kind, for example, the exchanges such as they were described in the document dated the 13th of July. What would you say about that?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, when negotiations were underway, if the International Red Cross and UNPROFOR visited us, we would provide oral reports about the negotiations conducted with the commission. However, once an exchange had been agreed on and once a date for an exchange had been agreed on, then we would make sure to inform the International Red Cross and UNPROFOR of the fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go back to the document dated the 13th of July. Number 12 mentions one of the prisoners who was in Mehurici. What you have said, the HVO told you that they wanted one of the men in Mehurici. What were you going to do? Because if they say one of the prisoners, you didn't know who this prisoner was. It wasn't your intention to call the unit in Mehurici in order to ask them whether they had any prisoners? What did you intend to do in that specific situation since over the radio you were told that they wanted to exchange 12 men for 12 men. Among the 12 men, there was one who was in Mehurici and whose identity you did not know. What were you going to do in order to make sure that the exchange took place? Could you explain to us what you intended to do since you were provided with information over the radio, and apparently you were not aware of whether there were any prisoners in Mehurici. So what did you intend to do given that situation?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, when I was provided with this information via radiolink, and I assume that the information was not correct because had the information been correct, the HVO would have provided the actual name of the person concerned. However, although the information was not complete, through the command of the OG, I sent a letter to the unit in the Mehurici area requesting that they check to see whether they had any HVO members in detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute. You said that you contacted the OG command and requested that they send a letter to the unit in Mehurici. Is that correct? And I want to point out the following: You were supposed to carry out this exchange on that very same day. That's what the HVO wanted. Wouldn't it have been simpler to phone Mehurici to find out whether they had any prisoners there unless it wasn't possible to establish such contact with Mehurici at the time?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, let me make a correction. The negotiations by radiolink took place on the 12th of July. That's what it says in this letter. The exchange was to take place on the 13th of July. And I had enough time to go to the command and check whether this prisoner actually existed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And did the command do what was necessary to establish contact with Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did they say? Did they have any prisoners or not?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, but I'm not a hundred per cent sure, I think this was the zone of responsibility of the 306th Brigade. And we received a letter stating that this was the first time they had heard about something of this kind. They said that they didn't have any HVO members in detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have our break now, and we will resume at 5 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, we resume. The Judges have a few more questions for the witness. I'm going to give the floor to Judge Swart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I would like to put you a few questions on the exchange matter that we have been discussing this morning. I remember, and please correct me if I'm wrong, that you said this morning that the first exchange you were involved in was somewhere in August 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: What exchange are you referring to? An exchange with the HVO or an exchange with the Serbians and Montenegrins?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I'm referring to an exchange with the HVO, yes.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I can't recall the exact date. I know that the first exchange was the one that I have spoken about today. This exchange involved Zarko Andric, also known as Zuti.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: We have been given documents you made on an exchange on the 16th August of 1993. Was that the first exchange that took effect in your period of activities, or has there been an exchange before?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: This exchange which took place on the 15th of August 1993 was not the first one with the HVO. The first exchange with the HVO was the one that involved Zuti when I handed over his relative, Dominic Andric to him. I can't remember the date, but I remember that this was the first exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Do you remember the date when the exchange with the body of Dominic Andric took place? Was it also in August? Was it in July?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Again, I don't remember the date. It could not have taken place in August because it was this exchange that took place in August. This, the first one must have been earlier. Whether it was a month before or not, I don't know. I only know that this exchange involved the dead body of Dominic Andric, an HVO fighter. There were also some prisoners of war involved. There were seven on our side and seven on their side, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Okay, let's go back to the documents you have been shown. This is, first of all, the document P655. You have been shown the document before. And if you still have it, please take it. We have been discussing this document before, and you said, well, I signed it on the bottom at the right-hand side, and Alagic signed it on the top of the right-hand side, and I suppose that the signature at the left-hand side on the bottom is the signature of Mr. Beba. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. However, my signature is missing. The only thing you see here is the stamp of the commission for exchanges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: That's right. Now, you told us about a conversation you had with the commander Alagic, and he asked you details on all the 12 persons to be exchanged. And when you discussed number 6, Mr. Kohal, he said he should not be included in the exchange. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: So he disappeared from the list, I suppose. My question is the following: If Alagic says he should not be exchanged -- included in the exchange, why did you not make a new document and let them sign the new document?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Well, the commander, Alagic, at that time had a lot of work and many tasks. It was very difficult to get a hold of him when he was free to talk to you. You could not get a hold of him at all times. He was moving around a lot. And it was the common practice for me to first do the negotiations, and then inform him in writing as to what had been discussed. After that, he would give me his consent for the exchange. I believe that there must be a document informing the units on the lines facing the HVO, that there would be an exchange on a certain date, and this was in view of the cease-fire. There must have been a document. I don't see it here. This new document must have been contained the exact list of the names of the people who would be exchanged. Those are the only persons who were allowed to approach the exchange line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Why did he not put a line through number 6? Why did he not simply omit number 6 from the list together with putting his signature?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: There was time, and there must have been a document stating the names of those to be exchanged. This had to be done in order to regulate the cease-fire during the exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Why not make a new document, then?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I believe that it was made. We don't have it, but it must have been drafted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Why did not you yourself put a line through number 6 in this document?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I had a notebook. In my notebook, I recorded what was said during the negotiations. And I used the notebook when I drafted reports for my commander. I suppose that I crossed that name in my notebook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I'm, of course, asking you this because we have been given a document with an official signature of you -- not of you, of Beba and Alagic at the same time, which includes number 6. So you are telling us there is a new document probably which does not contain number 6. But this is a document which on the face of it sounds that number 6 was included. Let me go back to the exchange on the 12th of July. You said there was no exchange on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I apologise. I would like to add something. This is not the final list for exchange. This is just the HVO proposal. The final list of people to be exchanged must have been submitted to the command on the same day. Following that, an order on cease-fire must have been issued in order to provide for the exchange. Maybe this is why there's no document number or it was not written on a letterheaded paper. Because this was just a preliminary document that was drafted immediately after the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did an exchange then take place at all?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes, it did. But this person was not included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You mean now number 6 of your list?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to the name under number 6. I can see this in the second document which is the report on exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: There is no interpretation of what you said. Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: We have this second document which is the information on the exchange. This exchange took place on the 16th of August 1993 in a place called Donje Puticevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: So you would say that the exchange that was intended to take place on the 13th of July was in effect realised in August 16 or 18. I don't know the date exactly. The 16th.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes. This is the exchange, and you can see that from the list of names of the people who were included in the exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Well, I've had an opportunity to compare the two lists during the break. But I think basically these are different lists, except one name.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: After the negotiations which took place on the 12th of July, this was the first exchange. Certain names had been altered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: It's difficult to understand because you said before that even before this exchange on the 16th, there was another exchange which a body of the son of a person you knew was also included, and that you recalled must have been somewhere in the beginning of August. But coming to your point, I see only different names with the exception of one to the extent I have been able to study the two lists.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: I can repeat, having heard what you said, that these lists are different. Just give me a moment. Muhamed Kohen was on the original list. Hasan Beganovic as well. Some detainees that I requested were not exchanged. We also kept some because no final agreement was reached. Some members of the HVO were not exchanged. They were kept in custody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Let's agree that number 1 on the list of 15 August mentions Hasan Beganovic, and he was on your list of 12 July, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And he's also on the list of the 16th, which is concerned with people that have been exchanged.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: A correction, please. On the 15th of August, there was another radio contact. And the lists were exchanged again, the list of people who were supposed to be included. It was only on the 16th that the actual exchange took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: There is also, as you said, a Muhamed on the list of the 15th, a certain Kahal Muhamed, and he's also on the list of the 16th, and there he's number 30.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: On your list of the 12th, there is one Muhamed, and that is number 5, Muhamed Kohen. And there is one Kohal, that's number 6, bus his name is Mustafa, and that's the Syrian. So I don't know -- quite know --

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: There must have been a typo. The person who was exchanged was Muhamed Kohen. I remember this person. He is still living in Travnik, or in Vitez. He is about 60 years of age. At that time, he was a civilian, not an army member.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Turn to the other side of the coin, people who have been exchanged on the 16th to the Croat side. You have a number of persons, and as far as I can see, none of them corresponds with the persons on your list of the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR SEFER
utterances.text: A number of the names which were on the list of the 12th were later omitted from the other list. The reason was the fact that the Croatian side did not include our fighters who were in their prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I now want to show you a new document you have not seen before. It's P399. And it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move into private session, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are back in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that we're back in open session, I'd like to ask the Prosecution -- I asked the Prosecution whether they had any further questions. They said they did not. I then gave the floor to Defence counsel, and Defence counsel also told me that had no additional questions. I'm now turning to the Defence. As far as the document that you want to tender into evidence is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the two documents dated the 15th of August and the 16th of August are the documents that we would like to have admitted into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have exhibit numbers for these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These two documents will have the same Exhibit number, DH346, and the English version will be DH346/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, I'd like to thank you. This concludes your testimony. We have concluded a few minutes before the end of the hearing. Thank you for answering the questions put to you by both parties and then by the Judges. I wish you a good trip home. And I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's also the Defence document belonging to General Kubura's Defence team, and they are requesting that this document be admitted into evidence. Mr. Registrar, do we have this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It appears we have the B/C/S version of this document. As far as I know, the Chamber should have the English version, at least I hope that that is the case. If not, I hope that Mr. Kubura's Defence can provide us with a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution during the break printed out another copy of that in English, and we can certainly provide this if there's no other English copy available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So Defence counsel will be tendering this document into evidence in both English and B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We have provided you with a copy. I think the Chamber has it. And we will ensure that we have other copies after the hearings. We have spoken about this with the Prosecution in the course of the break, and I don't think they have any objections of it being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar, could we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DK15, and the English version for this document DK15/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the Defence counsel now inform me of the schedule for the following week.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since you suggested that when we refer to witnesses who still haven't stated whether they will be requesting protective measures or not, could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are back in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we're in open session, we were discussing the schedule for next week. If there is -- if there are no other items to be raised, no other issues to be raised, I will see everyone at the hearing on Monday at 2.15.
